question: What is the penalty for using the ISI mark without a licence?
expected_answer: Section 29(3) of the BIS Act, 2016: contravening Section 17 is punishable with imprisonment up to two years, or fine of not less than two lakh rupees for the first contravention and not less than five lakh rupees for subsequent contraventions, which may extend up to ten times the value of goods, or both.

question: What does Section 17 of the BIS Act prohibit?
expected_answer: Section 17 prohibits manufacturing, importing, distributing, selling, hiring, leasing, storing or exhibiting for sale goods notified under Section 16(1) without a Standard Mark under a valid licence, or applying a Standard Mark when the goods do not conform to the standard.

question: Can a BIS officer search premises and seize goods that bear a fake standard mark?
expected_answer: Yes. Under Section 28 of the BIS Act, a certification officer who has reason to believe goods involved in a contravention of section 11, 14(6)/(8), 15 or 17 are hidden in any place, premises or vehicle may enter and search it and seize such goods.

question: If a company commits an offence under the BIS Act, who is held responsible?
expected_answer: Under Section 30, every director, manager, secretary or other officer in charge of and responsible for the company's business at the time, the authorised representative, and the company itself are deemed guilty and liable to be proceeded against.

question: Is the offence under Section 29 of the BIS Act cognizable?
expected_answer: Yes, the offence under section 29 is cognizable (Section 29(4)).

question: What is a Standard Mark according to the BIS Act, 2016?
expected_answer: Section 2: 'Standard Mark' means the mark specified by the Bureau, and includes Hallmark, representing conformity of goods, article, process, system or service to a particular Indian Standard or to a standard established, adopted or recognised by the Bureau.

question: Can I copy and publish an Indian Standard on my website?
expected_answer: No. Section 11 of the BIS Act prohibits publishing, reproducing or recording any Indian Standard or part of it, or any other BIS publication, without the authorisation of the Bureau.

question: Under which section can the Central Government make BIS certification compulsory for a product?
expected_answer: Section 16 of the BIS Act: after consulting the Bureau, the Central Government may by order direct compulsory use of the Standard Mark for notified goods, articles, processes, systems or services, e.g. in the public interest, for safety or health.

question: Can an offence under the BIS Act be compounded, and what is the limit?
expected_answer: Yes, offences may be compounded by an officer authorised by the Director General; the sum shall not exceed the maximum fine under section 29, and a later offence after three years from compounding is treated as a first offence.

question: Can I use the words 'Indian Standard' in my company name without permission?
expected_answer: No. Section 26 prohibits using, without the Bureau's previous permission and with a view to deceive, any name resembling the Bureau's name or containing the expression 'Indian Standard' or its abbreviation.

question: What is the application fee for a BIS product certification licence?
expected_answer: Rs. 1000 application fee; an inspection fee of Rs. 7,000 per man day is paid before the preliminary inspection; after the decision to grant, an annual licence fee of Rs. 1000 plus the minimum marking fee for the product.

question: How long does BIS take to grant a licence under option 1 and option 2?
expected_answer: Option 1: the grant of licence is expected to be completed within 90 days of receipt of the application; option 2: within 30 days, provided documents, assessment and product conformity are satisfactory at first instance.

question: How old can the test reports be when I apply for a licence under option 2?
expected_answer: Test reports must not be more than 90 days old (from date of issue to receipt of the application). With multiple reports, the latest must be within 90 days and the oldest within 180 days. They must be from BIS / BIS-recognised or empanelled labs.

question: When and how do I apply for renewal of my BIS licence?
expected_answer: Through the BIS portal (Manak Online) in Form-XII with relevant documents, preferably two months before the validity date. A licence may be renewed for up to five years.

question: My licence validity has already expired. Can I still renew it?
expected_answer: Yes, within 90 days after the validity date, by paying an additional late fee of ₹5,000; the decision to renew may be deferred for up to 90 days from the validity date.

question: How do I add a new variety or size to my existing ISI licence?
expected_answer: Apply for change in scope of licence in Form-XIV with the fee and documents; Rs. 5,000 per variety (or per group of varieties). If infrastructure is unchanged and the variety is in the same sampling group, third-party test reports are not required. The change is endorsed in Form-XV.

question: What are the reasons for which BIS can reject a licence application?
expected_answer: Under regulation 4(6) of the CA Regulations, e.g. samples not offered within 30 days, sample failing independent testing (second time), lack of testing facilities or technical personnel, corrective actions not taken in time, unpaid dues, tampered documents, unethical practices, major deviation in facilities, not assisting the certification officer, repeated FT non-conformity.

question: Will BIS give me notice before rejecting my application?
expected_answer: Yes. A rejection notice of not less than 21 days is given before rejecting an application, and the applicant can respond; if the explanation is not satisfactory the application is rejected.

question: What documents are required with an application for an ISI licence?
expected_answer: The BIS check-list requires e.g. a completely filled application form; name and address matching the Government registration document; status (large/small scale, with registration certificate for small units); the Indian Standard and varieties; manufacturing and testing facilities; test reports; and other items listed in the check-list.

question: Can an importer apply for a BIS licence on behalf of a foreign manufacturer?
expected_answer: No. Under FMCS the application must be made by the foreign manufacturer only; the foreign applicant must nominate an Authorized Indian Representative (AIR).

question: What happens if my product fails in testing after I get the licence?
expected_answer: Non-conformity is handled under the non-conformity guidelines: review of performance, corrective action, risk assessment, possible product recall, suspension (SUS), revocation of suspension, or cancellation.

question: Can small (MSME) manufacturers use shared testing facilities instead of their own lab?
expected_answer: Yes. BIS guidelines allow MSMEs to use Cluster Based Test Facilities (CBTF) / common test facilities under Scheme-I.

question: Is BIS certification compulsory for Sulphate Resisting Portland Cement?
expected_answer: Yes, IS 12330 under Scheme I (ISI mark), Cement (Quality Control) Order, 2003, S.O. 191(E) dated 17 Feb 2003.

question: Is BIS certification compulsory for LED lamps? Which IS number and which QCO?
expected_answer: Yes, self-ballasted LED lamps, IS 16102 (Part 1), under Scheme II (Compulsory Registration Scheme), Electronics & IT Goods (Requirements for Compulsory Registration) Order.

question: Which standard applies to TMT steel bars for concrete reinforcement and is ISI compulsory?
expected_answer: IS 1786 (high strength deformed steel bars and wires for concrete reinforcement), compulsory under Scheme I via the Steel and Steel Products (Quality Control) Order.

question: Do toys need the ISI mark? Which standard and order?
expected_answer: Yes. Safety of Toys, e.g. IS 9873 (Part 1), under the Toys (Quality Control) Order, 2020, S.O. 853(E) dated 25 February 2020 (with amendments).

question: Is packaged drinking water under compulsory BIS certification?
expected_answer: Yes, IS 14543 (packaged drinking water, other than packaged natural mineral water), notified under FSSAI Prohibition & Restriction on Sales Regulations, 2011 (GSR 759(E)/760(E)).

question: What is the IS number for two-wheeler rider helmets and which QCO covers them?
expected_answer: IS 4151:2015, Helmet for riders of Two Wheeler Motor Vehicles (Quality Control) Order, 2020, S.O. 4252(E) dated 26/11/2020.

question: Is IS 2347 compulsory? What product is it?
expected_answer: IS 2347:2017 is Domestic Pressure Cooker, compulsory under the Domestic Pressure Cooker (Quality Control) Order, 2020 (S.O. 294(E) dated 21/01/2020).

question: Do plugs and socket outlets need BIS certification?
expected_answer: Yes, IS 1293:2005, under the Plugs and Socket-Outlets and AC Direct Connected Static Prepayment Meters (Quality Control) Order, 2019.

question: Is IS 12330 the same product as IS 269?
expected_answer: No. IS 12330 is Sulphate Resisting Portland Cement and IS 269 is Ordinary Portland Cement; both are under the Cement (Quality Control) Order, 2003, S.O. 191(E).

question: Do electronic control gears for LED modules need CRS registration?
expected_answer: Yes, IS 15885 (Part 2/Sec 13), DC or AC supplied electronic control gear for LED modules, under Scheme II (CRS), Electronics & IT Goods Order.

question: What is HUID in hallmarked gold jewellery?
expected_answer: HUID (Hallmark Unique Identification) is a six-digit alphanumeric number, unique for each hallmarked item and traceable; it is one of the components of the hallmark.

question: How can a customer verify the HUID of jewellery?
expected_answer: Using the 'Verify HUID' feature in the BIS CARE app, which also shows the jeweller's registration details.

question: What marks make up the hallmark on gold jewellery?
expected_answer: Since 1 July 2021, three marks: the BIS logo, the purity in caratage and fineness, and the six-digit alphanumeric HUID.

question: What is hallmarking?
expected_answer: Hallmarking is the accurate determination and official recording of the proportionate content of precious metal in precious metal articles (as per IS 15820); hallmarks are official marks guaranteeing purity or fineness.

question: Which precious metals are hallmarked in India?
expected_answer: At present two: gold and silver.

question: How can I complain about a fake ISI-marked product?
expected_answer: Complaints are handled by CMED; they can be made offline or online through the BIS CARE app or the Standard Promotion Portal / online complaint registration, and are investigated for redressal.

question: What does the BIS (Hallmarking) Regulations, 2018 cover?
expected_answer: Three chapters: grant of registration for jewellers, recognition of Assaying and Hallmarking Centres, and grant of licence for refineries.

question: Should each earring in a pair have its own hallmark?
expected_answer: Yes, each article in a pair and all detachable parts should have a hallmark with different HUIDs.

question: How do I register under IBS?
expected_answer: BIS (not IBS): for an Indian manufacturer this is grant of licence under Scheme-I, applied online on Manak Online with the application fee, factory inspection and testing (option 1 or 2).

question: What documents are required to complete the IBS registration process?
expected_answer: As per the BIS application check-list: completed application form, registration documents, IS and varieties, facilities, test reports, etc.

question: What are the main steps to get started with BIS for a new business?
expected_answer: Identify the IS, check if compulsory, set up manufacturing and testing, apply online on Manak Online with fees, factory visit and sample testing, grant of licence and fees.

question: IBS licence fees kitne hai?
expected_answer: Application fee Rs. 1000, inspection fee Rs. 7,000 per man day, annual licence fee Rs. 1000 plus minimum marking fee.

question: what is BSI mark and how get it
expected_answer: BIS Standard Mark (ISI mark) is obtained by grant of licence under Scheme-I via Manak Online.

question: What is the alternative process if my product does not meet the eligibility criteria for option 2 (e.g. no third-party lab)?
expected_answer: The case can be processed under option-1 or, where there is no third-party laboratory, on factory-testing (FT) basis with the approval of Head (BO); foreign manufacturers are always option-1.

question: What should I do if my licence application is incomplete, and what are the consequences?
expected_answer: Deficiencies must be corrected within the time given; if corrective actions are not taken within the stipulated time, the application may be processed for rejection after a rejection notice of not less than 21 days.

question: Compare the main BIS certification schemes (Scheme I, Scheme II, Scheme IV, FMCS).
expected_answer: Scheme I: licence to use the Standard Mark (ISI) with factory inspection/testing; Scheme II: registration (CRS) based on self-declaration and test reports for electronics/IT; Scheme IV: certificate of conformity; FMCS: Scheme I for foreign manufacturers with an AIR.

question: How do I update my business name or address on my BIS licence after registration?
expected_answer: Inform BIS with relevant documents: shifting/change of address needs documents for the new premises as at grant of licence; change of name, management or ownership: details with documents are collected and the change is endorsed in the licence.

question: If BIS raises objections on my application, how much time do I get and what happens next?
expected_answer: Before rejection, a rejection notice of not less than 21 days is given; the applicant may reply in person or through a representative; if not satisfactory, the application is rejected and closure communicated.

question: हॉलमार्किंग क्या है और HUID कैसे चेक करें?
expected_answer: Hallmarking = official determination and recording of precious metal content; HUID is a 6-digit alphanumeric code verifiable with 'Verify HUID' in the BIS CARE app.

question: BIS लाइसेंस के लिए आवेदन शुल्क कितना है?
expected_answer: Application fee Rs. 1000; inspection fee Rs. 7,000 per man day; annual licence fee Rs. 1000 plus minimum marking fee.

question: बिना लाइसेंस के ISI मार्क लगाने पर क्या सज़ा है?
expected_answer: Section 29(3): imprisonment up to two years, fine at least 2 lakh (first) / 5 lakh (subsequent), up to ten times value of goods.

question: क्या खिलौनों के लिए BIS प्रमाणन अनिवार्य है?
expected_answer: Yes, toys under IS 9873 via Toys (Quality Control) Order, 2020.

question: लाइसेंस का नवीनीकरण कैसे करें?
expected_answer: Renewal in Form-XII via the BIS portal, preferably two months before validity; late renewal within 90 days with ₹5,000 late fee.

question: What is the capital of France?
expected_answer: REFUSE (not covered)

question: Write me a poem about the monsoon.
expected_answer: REFUSE (not covered)
